6	GS US TMT .. 10 things ..
7	Sentiment check .. NDX now up 7 of 8 sessions, registering new ATHs along the way; that said, I would describe investor sentiment as reserved optimism … with a heavy dose of angst and fatigue – see GS sentiment indicator in firmly negative territory and market breadth at the lowest levels since 2000. To be clear, the good AI / Tech days over the last couple of weeks have felt great (… “we’re back” types of vibes), that said, it has been hard to discern if the recent Tech/AI strength has been a pure, bottoms up led rally (think; Muse / Personal Agents + model updates + ROIC confidence), or, simply, a hard-to-rely on macro led rally as Rates and Oil briefly opened the door for risk to trade freely post the recent FOMC meeting. In turn, “gross and net” management remains in focus for investors (especially as we kick off 4Q trading this week) – though, under the surface of a soggy risk backdrop, it is worth noting that the market has started to be a bit more directional in under-the-surface tilts with signs of the ‘AI’ (inclusive of inference economy names) vs the “rest” again evident in price action – think: NDX > SPX for 4 straight weeks (or, even, SPX > S&P Equal-weight for 18 of 21 sessions). 
8	Market breadth has recently plunged: While AI strength has kept the headline S&P 500 relatively resilient, the median stock in the index trades 16% below its 52-week high, dragging market breadth to its lowest level since the Dot-Com Bubble.
9	Source: GS. GIR. Past performance is not indicative of future results. link
10	Top inbounds last week … views on AMZN here given agentic commerce? .. are Semis back?.. set-up into MU? Do people like DRAM? .. .. what’s the next move for Security / Data Infra? .. why is AAPL at ATHs if AI is finding its footing? … fav Internet/Services name to buy on weakness? … can MSFT have a moment here? .. whats been up with CSCO/Optical names? .. Why are markets strong despite Rates ?.. 
11	Trending .. names that are now in overbought territory (per 14-day RSIs >70): AMD, INTC, VICR, TWLO, OKTA, DT, RNG, NTSK, ZS, MKTX … vs … oversold territory (14-day RSIs <30): CALX, DY, ALKT, NAVN, INTU, GEN, PAYX, VRRM, WU, KLAR, FIS, STUB, ABNB, YELP, BKNG, CHWY, CMCSA, LAMR .. 
12	Compute Semis …. CPUs > XPUs … with INTC and AMD each up 35%+ in the month of September (and the SOX up 10%), investors are trying to figure out what it will take for NVDA (up only +2% on the month) and AVGO (down 5% on the month) to 'catch-up' to the index, let alone their 'compute' peers' in INTC & AMD (.. is it as simple as ‘thematic’ trading alongside the consumer agent narrative?..) .. would note, even looking more closely at NVDA vs AVGO, while NVDA still trades at a 1x-2x discount to AVGO on fwd P/E (bottom chart), a relatively wide spread has opened up in their performance (top chart) as AVGO is one of the few semiconductor names I could find that currently sits below its 200-dma... 
13	Source: Goldman Sachs FICC & Equities, Bloomberg, as of September 2026. Past performance is not indicative of future results.
14	TTWO … we are now 53 days out from the launch of GTA 6 .. yet .. TTWO just closed near ~10 year lows relative to the s&P500 (chart below) .. inbounds have started to pick-up if worth revisiting ahead of the GTA 6 launch or if the catalyst has already played out / been fully priced in .. 
15	Source: Goldman Sachs FICC & Equities, Bloomberg, as of September 2026. Past performance is not indicative of future results.
16	Semis watch … while Semis have been caught up in a difficult period for much of calendar 3Q (Semis down -11% in 3Q with names like KLAC / AMAT / LRCX down 30%+), the group (Semis, SOX) is quietly up 4 weeks in a row, burning off some of the Summer malaise and driving an uptick in investor inbounds about the likelihood of another run down the stretch of 2026. As of late, the emergence of the Consumer Personal Agent narrative has started to give investors’ some ability to pattern match against the 1H ‘playbook’ around Agents in the Enterprise (e.g. easier to play through semis than it is to pick the winner up the stack – model or agent?) .. though, we may need to see durable macro relief for the rally to sustain as the fwd P/E multiple of the SOX has been inversely correlated to the moves in Oil prices.
17	… and yes, Semiconductor valuations appear to embed particularly skeptical views regarding the sustainability of current earnings strength (chart below)
18	Source: GS. GIR. Past performance is not indicative of future results.
19	‘Inference Economy’ … trending .. it has been impressive (and understandable) to see the market continue to reward ‘inference’ economy names (asset light, AI levered plays – think Cyber Security or Data Infra names) as these are names that bulls believe can grow through any potential future capex gyrations (or, at least, are largely immune from subtle rate of changes on ASPs or S/D). While we have very much been in a “rising tide lifts all boats” backdrop for names tied to capex-light inference workloads – we do sense some emerging debates on entry points and valuations (e.g. perhaps time for some well-earned digestion?), especially as market leaders like Cloudflare (NET) bump into the upper end of their trading ranges (chart below) … 
20	Source: Goldman Sachs FICC & Equities, Bloomberg, as of September 2026. Past performance is not indicative of future results.
21	MU … earnings preview .. Micron set to report earnings on Wednesday evening – positioning feels relatively balanced to me (though, worth noting that MU is just ~10% below ATHs vs Samsung & Hynix stilly ~20-40% below the highs) with investors broadly expecting the mix towards SCAs to somewhat limit the beat size (.. at least relative to MU beating EPS by 10-30% over the last ~6 quarters). Talking points for investors into the print: 1) Nov qtr revenues guide relative to the street up +10% q/q (e.g. magnitude of y/y and q/q deceleration), 2) any additional updates around SCAs .. 3) mix of cap allocation into FY27: capex vs capital returns .. 4) HBM market shares .. 5) industry s/d (esp re: China) .. note: MU’s stock price (white) has now fallen below MU earnings (EPS) estimate trend (orange) – chart below …
22	Source: Goldman Sachs FICC & Equities, Bloomberg, as of September 2026. Past performance is not indicative of future results.
23	ACN preview .. earnings Thurs morning (10/1) .. investor sentiment remains guarded here (short interest firmly near 5 year highs, per Bloomberg – chart below) with Accenture having traded lower on 13 of 18 prints t+1; big picture, investors are debating Accenture’s long-term growth rate in the AI era (... esp relative to consensus forecasts that call for revenues to re-accelerate towards ~5% in FY28/29) .. via GIR preview – published back on 9/11/26: “We believe investors remain negatively positioned on the stock and the IT Services group ahead of earnings on October 1. In addition to the persistent consensus view that AI poses a potential structural risk to the IT Services industry (which continues to pressure P/E multiples for the group), we believe ongoing demand headwinds (in part due to the Mideast conflict) and crowding out of Services spending have weighed on client demand trends through August. Given the lack of visibility and management's need to guide to FY27 with limited information, we modestly tick down our estimates to reflect ~1% organic growth in the coming year. We expect Accenture to deliver a largely in-line quarter and guide for FY27 revenue growth of 3% - 4% in CC, along with 10-30bps of operating margin expansion and EPS growth of 6% - 8%.” [GIR preview]
24	Source: Goldman Sachs FICC & Equities, Bloomberg, as of September 2026. Past performance is not indicative of future results.
